rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, three field studies 2004-2005 at Citra FL with own yield, soil water and leaching data. Q2: Table 3 Study 3, soil moisture sensor-based (QIC/ECH2O capacitance probe) treatments SUR1 and SDI gave marketable yields of 27.6 and 26.9 Mg/ha versus 20.5 for the once-daily timed SURtime; Section 3.3, in Study 2 the drier set point (SUR1) reduced yield 12.4% attributed to water stress during fruit development. Q4: Fig. 2 TDR soil water content shows timed irrigation produced large VWC fluctuations and drainage below the root zone (Fig. 1B), with N displacement in the profile (Fig. 4) linked to lower dry matter and yield; Section 3.3 soil solution nitrate dilution under higher irrigation. Q8: Section 3.1, three unprotected frost events in 2005 reduced harvests, growth and yield relative to 2004. Q9: Tables 2-3 report coefficients of variation for yield; Fig. 1 bars are 1 S.E.
rows.notes: Technology is sensor-based drip scheduling on plastic-mulched zucchini, matching the claim. Yield measured by harvest only (Q3 no). Single site, soil and crop (Q5, Q6 no). Authors say soil water availability was a primal component of production and that the lower set point caused stress, but do not state an explicit requirement for the yield effect (Q7 no, borderline).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field experiments with lysimeters and soil cores. Q2: Section 3.4 and Fig. 1C, sensor-controlled SDI leached 1.7-2.4 kg N/ha versus 35-45 kg/ha under the timed SURtime treatment; abstract says sensor-based control reduced irrigation and minimized N leaching. Q3: Section 2.2, nitrate leaching assessed by zero-tension drainage lysimeters (Fig. 1C) and independently by soil coring to 0.9 m showing N displacement in the profile (Fig. 4). Q4: Fig. 2 TDR soil water content and Fig. 1B drainage volumes (62 mm for SUR2/SURtime vs 14 mm for SDI) measured as the pathway to leaching. Q7: Conclusions, sensor-based irrigation may give consistent leaching reduction when soil volumetric water content is maintained within the field capacity threshold. Q9: Fig. 1 bars 1 S.E. for cumulative leaching; soil solution nitrate given as mean plus/minus deviation in Section 3.3.
rows.notes: Note the sensor-based SUR2 (higher set point) leached 20-26 kg/ha and drained a volume similar to SURtime, so the leaching reduction depends on set point and drip placement. Limitations: SUR1 drainage not monitored and rainfall assumed negligible, but these are not framed as limitations of the result (Q8 no).

rows.evidence: Q1: Own field studies, Sections 2-3. Q2: Table 3 Study 3, SUR1 (sensor-based) vs SURtime (once-daily timed): yield 27.6 vs 20.5 Mg/ha (about 35%), IWUE 16.1 vs 4.3 kg/m3 (about 274%), NUE 37.1 vs 26.5% (about 40%), exactly the figures in the passage. Q4: Fig. 2 soil water content, Fig. 1B drainage, Fig. 4 soil nitrate displacement measured and linked to lower dry matter and N accumulation under high-volume timed irrigation. Q8: Section 3.1, unprotected frost events in 2005 reduced harvest number, growth and yield. Q9: Table 3 coefficients of variation; Fig. 1 S.E. bars.
rows.notes: Figures in the passage reproduce Study 3 Table 3. Single site, soil and crop; plot scale. No explicit requirement stated for the yield effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Own field studies. Q2: Table 1 and Conclusions, sensor-based treatments applied 160-329 mm versus 482 mm for the timed treatment, a 33-80% reduction in irrigation water; Table 3 IWUE 16.1 (SUR1) and 16.8 (SDI) vs 4.3 kg/m3 (SURtime). Q4: Section 3.4 and Fig. 2, TDR measurements show sensor control applied water only when VWC fell below the set point, reducing VWC fluctuation and percolation, with drainage volumes measured in lysimeters (Fig. 1B). Q9: Table 3 coefficient of variation for IWUE; Fig. 1A cumulative irrigation.
rows.notes: Irrigation volume measured by flowmeters only (one method). No limitation stated specifically for the water-use result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Own plot trials at Citra FL. Q2: Table 1 and Conclusions, capacitance-probe (ECH2O/QIC) sensor-controlled drip on plastic-mulched zucchini reduced irrigation 33-80% versus the timed treatment (172/160 mm vs 482 mm); Table 3 IWUE 16.1-16.8 vs 4.3 kg/m3. Q4: Fig. 2 TDR soil water dynamics and Fig. 1B drainage volumes measured, showing sensor control reduced VWC fluctuations and percolation. Q9: Table 3 C.V. for IWUE; Fig. 1 S.E. bars.
rows.notes: Small-plot study matching the passage (zucchini, capacitance sensors). One measurement method for water applied; single site and crop; no stated limitation on the water-saving result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Own plot trials. Q2: Table 3 Study 3, sensor-triggered SUR1 and SDI yields 27.6 and 26.9 Mg/ha versus 20.5 Mg/ha for timed irrigation, a significant improvement; Conclusions report similar or higher yields with sensor-based SDI. Q4: Fig. 2 soil water content, Fig. 1B drainage and Fig. 4 soil nitrate displacement measured and linked to reduced dry matter and N accumulation under timed irrigation. Q8: Section 3.1, 2005 frosts reduced harvests, growth and yield. Q9: Table 3 C.V. for marketable yield.
rows.notes: Yield improvement held for the sensor treatments with the lower set point; the sensor treatment with the higher set point (SUR2) yielded no more than timed irrigation in 2005. Single site and crop, plot scale.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study compares soil-moisture-sensor-controlled drip (with surface and subsurface placement) against a once-daily timed treatment for zucchini on plastic mulch on sandy soil; all claim rows concern the sensor-based scheduling, which the study tested directly.
